commits.note: credential model corrected: server-side env first

note: design correction (user): OS keychain is NOT a valid credential place for a WEB APP. Corrected model: credentials are SERVER-SIDE, environment-injected (12-factor — deployment platform / secrets manager sets env at runtime; the adapter runs server-side; the browser client never holds the key). Registry chain reordered env-first: env:ANN_LLM_API_KEY || keychain:ann/llm-api-key. macOS keychain + cred! demoted to DEV-ONLY local-CLI convenience (documented in credentials.ts + AGENTS.md). Production credential path = server env.

PRODUCT-FORM DECISION (by ian): LOCAL WEB APP — local-first, client-server architecture, packaged together. The client (browser UI) supports local AND remote servers; the server runs locally by default and owns the engine + the journey (single-writer store); both ship in one package. Implications: credentials are SERVER-side (local server: env or OS keychain both valid; remote server: env/secrets-manager) — the client never holds them; the human-interface adapter (S8) renders web HTML to the local/remote server; the journey tree lives on the server; multi-user remains deferred (a remote server could serve multiple clients later). The web-UI target in architecture (locked @ fcfa661) is now refined to this topology — record in the architecture doc when S8 starts.

config file layer (local-first): ~/.config/ann/config.json (ANN_CONFIG override for tests/packaging) — provider/model/baseUrl/apiKey/maxTokens; resolution env > config > keychain/fallback; chmod 600, outside the repo, apiKey masked everywhere; `ann config` (masked show) + `ann config! set <key> <value>`. Trust model: like ~/.aws/credentials (plaintext at rest, 600, local); keychain stays the more-secure option. Suite 109 pass. Demo: config! set apiKey -> providers shows SET (config file, masked).

multi-project support (user-requested): commands no longer assume cwd — project root resolves via --project <name> | ANN_PROJECT | walk-up to journey/ (git-like) | config.currentProject; each project has its OWN journey + store (one store per project); user config ~/.config/ann/config.json holds projects[] + currentProject + credentials (per-user, shared across projects); `ann project` (read) + `ann project! add|use|remove`. Lazy vocab + lazy store (chdir before any store access — project cmds run from any dir). Suite 112 pass. cwd-discovery + flag + env + current verified live.

LAYOUT DECISION (by ian): everything ann-owned in a project lives under <project>/.ann/ — journey/ + docs/ + rules/ (subtle, machine-owned, no hand-edits). Root-level journey/docs/rules become compat symlinks to .ann/* so recorded paths + relative artifact links keep resolving. Recognition marker becomes .ann/ (legacy journey/ accepted). ~/.ann/ stays the per-USER app config (user state vs per-project state, both named .ann by design). docs/ is ann-owned content surfaced via ann (specs/result/detail commands), not user-edited — decided subtle over visible.
